summary:
# NOTES: *A Little Irish Girl* (J. M. Callwell)

Single novel, no separate books. Telegraphic form.

## Cast
- **Norah O'Brien**: 11, youngest, small, short black hair like pony mane, turned-up nose, wide mouth, dark-blue "Irish eyes", shabby black mourning frock, impulsive, mischievous ringleader, proud of Irish name (spells without h). Sang "St. Patrick was a gentleman".
- **Anstace O'Brien**: elder sister, gentle, practical, Irish-English; governess to Dr. Trafford's family in London; named after godmother Cousin Ansey; "our mother was an Englishwoman."
- **Roderick O'Brien**: eldest, tall, dark, 21+, college honours, gave up bar, lawyer's clerk, cough/weak lungs, later writer (articles for magazines, *Piccadilly*), Irish eldest brother.
- **Manus O'Brien**: 12, brother, close-cropped "bullet head", sunburnt, at cheap school in Kent (Dr. Ford's), friend of Bodkin Major (Galway, hunts).
- **Piers O'Brien**: late father, journalist, genial, Irish accent, died autumn ~6 months before; buried in London cemetery; half-brother of Nicholas.
- **Marion Belthorpe**: mother, English, died long before Norah's memory. Nicholas was engaged to her; she eloped with Piers the day before wedding; her father died from shock.
- **Uncle Nicholas O'Brien**: Piers's half-brother, ~60s+, white hair/brows, hooked nose, keen dark eyes, stooped, owner of Moyross Abbey and copper mine; vindictive, proud; kept a watercolour portrait of Marion (fair hair banded down).
- **Cousin Ansey (Anstace O'Brien)**: old relation, jilted by Hugh Masters (went to America); waited for him; went mad; asylum in Dublin 12 years; died; left Kilshane to Piers's family.
- **Kilshane**: small old house on cliffs, ~2 miles from Moyross, ~£100/yr, "The Hogan" tenancy, lawyer's keys.
- **Harry Wyndham**: 17-ish, grandnephew of Nicholas, hot-headed, sent to Austria/Carpathians for mining training; runs away home; later wants army (red coat).
- **Ella Wyndham**: gentle, fair, 16-ish, rides black pony **Sheila**; orphan of niece (Jess O'Brien's daughter's line) who died in India.
- **Miss Browne ("Brownie")**: tall, thin, stooped, near-sighted glasses, prim, former governess, nursed Ella's mother Mrs. Wyndham at Dinapore (cholera; Captain Wyndham died first); promised to stay with children; prejudiced vs Irish and O'Briens.
- **Mr. & Mrs. Lynch**: old rector (boxed Piers's ears over Latin) and trim wife; Roderick's friends.
- **Biddy**: Tom Hogan's sister, Kilshane servant, untidy, Irish brogue; hens in kitchen; later at Hogans'.
- **Tom Hogan**: Biddy's brother, former coachman of Cousin Ansey, now steward/farmhand; 7 orphans.
- **Lanty Hogan**: red-haired, freckled eldest orphan, poacher/fisherman/potheen-maker; accomplice of Manus.
- **Bride Hogan**: Lanty's sister, bashful maid at Kilshane.
- **Kat**: 2-year-old Hogan baby.
- **Connor**: car-driver, Ballyfin; his mother Mrs. Connor (quilted night-cap, pigs, potato scones, cannibal sow); son Thady.
- **Malachy Flanagan**: red-bearded still-operator on Drinane Head; orator for miners; his mother (old woman, red handkerchief).
- **M'Bain**: Scotch mine manager, brought in new machinery/methods, hated.
- **Captain Charles Lester, R.M.**: resident magistrate, big, sandy, jolly, red face.
- **Lady Louisa Butler**: of Dromore (14 Irish miles), white-haired, soft brogue, knew Piers.
- **Cartwright**: English butler at Moyross.
- **Dr. Hanlon**: doctor at Moyross.
- **Dr. Trafford**: London doctor (Roderick's cough).
- **Dr. & Mrs. Ford**: Manus's school principals.
- **Lily Allardyce**: Norah's school friend, pink-and-white, wealthy, parents chemical manufacturers, home Heron's Court, Hampshire; family went to Paris.
- **Miss Clarkson** (stately head, sanctum upstairs), **Miss Euphemia** (junior teacher, cap, pencil taps), **Miss Susan** (second Miss Clarkson), **Fräulein Glock** (German governess), **Constance Lane**, **Louisa** (flaxen girl), **Jane & Ellen** (maids).

## Places
Treherne House (N. London suburb, school; brass plate); Hampstead Heath (old home); Euston station; Dublin quays; Ballyfin (railway terminus, 12 Irish miles to Kilshane); Ennis (jail); Dromore; Moyross Abbey (ruins, cloisters, beech graveyard, Monks' Walk glen down to cove); Kilshane; Portkerin (cove, Lanty's coracle); Drinane Head (black promontory, tarn, still hovel, white stones as markers); Ballintaggart Cave (seal cave, "Seals' Parlour"); iron pier and mine (trollies, zigzag track); Clare (county); Connaught mentioned.

## Chronological events
**Ch I** (Treherne House, spring, 3 weeks before Easter holidays): Geography lesson (Turkey in Asia). Norah daydreams, "Tuesday fortnight" blunder, sent to bottom of class, must write lesson indoors. Lily consoles, promises gift. Norah's background: father died 6 months ago, Anstace the mother-figure, Roderick and Anstace sacrificed to keep Norah in school at reduced fees; Manus in Kent; Anstace governess; Roderick clerk. Lily promised to take Norah to Hampshire, but Lily's family goes to Paris instead.

**Ch II**: Parlour-maid calls Norah to drawing-room; Miss Euphemia relents. Anstace reveals legacy (Kilshane); Norah's joy; Roderick visited Moyross for Cousin Ansey's funeral; Uncle Nicholas turned white, didn't speak; Mr. Lynch took Roderick in. Feud story told by Anstace (Marion, Piers, elopement, father's death, Nicholas's wrath). Nicholas's copper mine rebuilt the estate. Anstace: "satisfied?" Roderick's cough; Dr. Trafford. Anstace visits Miss Clarkson's sanctum.

**Ch III**: Norah sings; in her mood, Lily gives sunflower pincushion. Norah says she'll go to Ireland. Tea-tray toboggan down upper staircase; Lily screams at Miss Clarkson's appearance; both fall; Norah's head bump. Norah's defiant speech. Whole school sees; Miss Clarkson kisses Norah, forgives "for this once".

**Ch IV**: Term ends; Lily leaves for Paris. Norah counts days on fingers. Roderick takes her to Euston; sea-sickness; Dublin wharf; Ballyfin at dusk; outside-car drive through bog; Norah sobs at ugliness. Atlantic roar. Driver's Irish speech. Tom carries Norah in; Biddy with turf torch: "Begorra... one of the O'Briens"; supper; sleep.

**Ch V**: Norah's first morning view. Anstace/Roderick explore; Roderick: "copper-mine... iron pier... Monks' Walk". Roderick saw Monks' Walk at funeral. Biddy's kitchen (hens, dog, kittens, turkey, lumber); dog licks frying-pan, Biddy throws candlestick. Anstace: "our mother was an Englishwoman... not find it natural that hens should lay in wine-coolers." Upstairs attic finds (silver with O'Brien crest, jewels, shawls, lavender). Biddy recounts Miss Ansey's life ("Hugh"); Tom's seven orphans; Lanty brings fish. Norah sees Tom as Biddy's brother. Biddy dismissed; Bride takes her place. Kilshane tidied, flowers; Anstace: "proud of our little home."

**Ch VI**: Mr. Lynch on Moyross: new Scotch manager M'Bain, machinery, skull-and-cross-bones on his door. Harry in Austria. Mrs. Lynch on Ella. Manus arrives (diphtheria at school; letter misspelled "diftheria"). Norah drives with Connor to Ballyfin; reunion with Manus. Visit to Mrs. Connor's pigs and potato scones. Sheila runs away near Kilshane gate; Roderick catches her at great risk. Ella: "I am Ella Wyndham... Moyross Abbey." Ella stays; Anstace nurses; Ella: "cousins". Lanty carries note to Moyross; Lanty's tales (seabirds, trout) to Manus. Tea; Miss Browne arrives, bonnet on backwards, table-cover as shawl. Ella leaves.

**Ch VII**: Miss Browne's view: O'Brien family as schemers; Ella's innocence; dislikes Irish. Carriage at Moyross; Ella tells uncle; Nicholas's reaction (paper-knife). Ella describes Anstace and Norah; sees Marion's portrait, Nicholas: "That is not the portrait of any O'Brien."

**Ch VIII**: Weeks pass (May–June). Manus–Lanty friendship; Norah jealous. Roderick dismisses Anstace's worries. Lanty plans seal hunt at Ballintaggart Cave at spring tide. Norah overhears at dairy window; runs to Portkerin; begs to come. Coracle trip past Moyross, mine pier. Cave; Lanty leaves Norah in recess; Manus shoots seal; seal knocks Manus down, tears sleeve; Lanty clubs seal. Norah alone, panics; Manus's halloos. Manus proud; Lanty: "ye're the first leddy that iver wint sale-huntin'".

**Ch IX**: Row home in dark; boat of men (Malachy red-bearded steersman, "thau" = yes); Lanty leaves them to go to Drinane Head. Lanty lands them at Moyross cove, dumps seal, rows away. Monks' Walk: white figure with arm raised; Manus fires at "3" — hits table-cloth on tree. Flee. Laundry maid weeps; Miss Browne scolds her; Ella intervenes; Miss Browne: "plot... English." Coachman leaves. Manus & Norah keep secret; Manus reveals Lanty's Drinane Head business. Home: supper; Roderick & Anstace late (horse shoe lost, forge delay); Manus's seal story; Norah ill that night.

**Ch X**: Next morning Anstace reports table-cloth gossip (warning to Nicholas). Uncle closes mine and sacks miners. Mr. Lynch: "bad winter". Manus's school return approaching. Lady Louisa's invitation to Dromore; Biddy wants old chariot; Roderick laughs. Captain Lester's note (seizure at Drinane; wants shake-down; "keep secret"). Dinner: Bride's blunders (mustard/sugar, cauliflower, croquettes, mashed potatoes spilled); Biddy at door; Manus winks. Lester tells Roderick his raid will be at five am. Manus tells Norah: Lanty's still on Drinane Head; Norah plans to warn.

**Ch XI**: Norah wakes; clock hall at 2:30, 3 am; wakes Manus, who refuses ("Lanty will look after himself"). Norah goes alone at dawn across moor, struggling through heather, bog, cliffs, sunrise. Finds tarn, hovel. Malachy and Lanty (eyes red, smoky). Norah warns. Still dismantled, sunk in tarn; whisky poured into stream. Men see police on heights; Malachy: "What'll we do wid the child?" Norah hidden: shawl, hat thrown away, pretends to be Malachy's daughter.

**Ch XII**: Lester and Roderick enter with four constables; search; Roderick doesn't recognize Norah. Malachy's mock: "Innicint dissitation!" Lester's warning speech. Men's sneers. Norah leaves; Malachy carries her on back to road edge; kisses her hand: "one o' the raal ould O'Briens". Norah promises secrecy. Roderick and Lester pass in dog-cart; Roderick nods. Roderick holds Norah at Kilshane door; Anstace scolds about eggs and muddy shoes. Lester at breakfast: "warning... by the winds"; suspects Lanty. Manus lies; signals Norah; she blushes. Manus blames Norah for going alone.

**Ch XIII**: Roderick and Anstace go to Dromore (Lady Louisa's). Manus and Norah go to mine at dusk (Manus: "wouldn't it be fun..."). Crowd of miners in works yard; Malachy on trolly harangues: "Nich'las O'Brien... lazy Irish pisants... Come on to Moyross... young Roderick O'Brien we'll have." Children hide in shed; crowd rushes past. Norah insists: "run to Moyross and warn Uncle Nicholas and Ella." Old women: "Musha!"

**Ch XIV**: Moyross dinner: Ella, Miss Browne, Harry (returned from Austria, defiant). Norah and Manus arrive, scratched, tell of mob; Harry dismisses it. Crowd arrives; shutters, bars; Harry arms Cartwright; Norah tries to speak; Harry refuses. Norah takes white quilt and candle from Uncle Nicholas (just arrived by stable-yard, mistakes her: "Who are you, child?"). Norah & Manus climb abbey; Norah in high window, quilt, candle; crowd flees. Norah falls from window. Ella, Nicholas: "Norah O'Brien" = Piers's boyhood resemblance. Side door; Norah and Manus out.

**Ch XV**: Manus returns, cries; "It was all Norah's idea." Harry and Cartwright carry Norah in. Doctor (Dr. Hanlon): concussion. Uncle sends telegram/carriage to Dromore. Dawn: Roderick & Anstace arrive; Nicholas sees Anstace as Marion ("Marion!").

**Ch XVI**: Roderick & Nicholas reconcile ("As if I had not wanted you all along!"). Nicholas: "Piers... only brother"; regrets not reconciling. Harry wants army; Nicholas consents. Ice sent, Dr. from Ennis. Ella nurses Norah. Lady Louisa visits. Malachy weeps on steps, rumour "goin' fast". Peace: M'Bain stays 3 months then Roderick takes charge; men accept machinery; Malachy's influence; Roderick's speech; crowd cheers. Miss Browne leaves after Roderick proposes to Ella in Monks' Walk (betrothal). Norah wakes in early autumn; asks for Lanty; Lanty promises no more potheen; Roderick offers Lanty under-gamekeeper job (Pat Lannigan). Norah tells Roderick about table-cloth and Lanty's secrets; Roderick laughs; Ella scolds Roderick. Uncle Nicholas: "Nothing ... alters your future prospects... heir"; Norah: "I told you so, Anstace"; Roderick rebukes; Nicholas defends Norah; Nicholas on Piers: "wish he were here". Anstace: "a year next week since he died... gathered in his old home."
